subtopics.title: What a GIS Is and the Two Kinds of Data

questions.question: A Geographical Information System is a computerised system that does five things with spatially referenced data:
options: Captures, stores, manipulates, analyses and displays it
Prints, laminates, folds, files and posts it
Measures, weighs, counts, sorts and deletes it
Draws, colours, labels, frames and hangs it

questions.question: The route number printed on a main road on the topographic map is an example of:
options: Attribute data — a fact attached to the feature, not its position

questions.question: A natural line feature on a topographic map is:
Which statement about vector and raster data is correct?
options: Raster builds features from points, lines and polygons
Vector and raster are two names for the same thing
Vector builds crisp shapes from points, lines and polygons; raster builds the scene from a grid of cells

questions.question: Data layering is best defined as:
options: Printing a map on several sheets of paper
Storing different kinds of information in separate layers that can be placed on top of one another
Saving a backup copy of the map

questions.question: A layer showing only rivers, dams and pans should be named the:
Why can separate GIS layers be combined without features shifting position?
options: All layers are georeferenced to the same coordinates
The computer stretches each layer to fit
Features are redrawn by hand each time
Only one layer may be viewed at a time

questions.question: When an exam question asks you to redraw and combine given layer sketches into one frame, the key rule is:
options: Enlarge every feature so it is easier to see
Copy every feature in its original position, overlapping where the originals overlap

questions.question: Buffering is:
options: Converting raster data to vector data
Drawing a zone of chosen width around a feature so the inside is treated differently from the outside
Zooming in on an unclear image

questions.question: Open land is kept empty between a town and an area of sinkholes and subsiding ground. The GIS term for this planning measure is:
options: Buffering — a no-build zone around the hazard

questions.question: Asking the system to show every clinic within ten kilometres of the taxi rank is an example of:
Data integration must happen before querying can work because:
options: Queries only run on paper maps
Queries need the printer switched on
Data from different sources must first be brought into one system on the same grid so layers can be searched together

subtopics.title: Resolution, Data Manipulation and the Way GIS Is Examined

questions.question: The clarity of an image, set by the size and number of its pixels, is called:
Of two photographs of the same area, the one with FEWER pixels will look:
options: Blurrier, because each pixel is larger and detail is lost
Sharper, because pixels are spread out

questions.question: An area on the orthophoto is unclear. Using data manipulation, how would you manipulate the scale to make the image clearer?
options: Make the scale smaller to show more ground
Make the scale larger — zoom in so the same ground fills more of the image
Convert the image to a table

questions.question: The GIS block in the mapwork question typically mixes which three question types?
options: Drawing contours, colouring layers and naming oceans
Vocabulary multiple choice, application to the mapped area, and a practical layer redraw

subtopics.title: The Burger That Explains the Whole System

questions.question: The burger comparison teaches that a GIS keeps information:
options: In separate layers made independently but viewed stacked together
In one flat drawing that cannot be split

questions.question: Your friend's position on the field is to spatial data what their name and phone number are to:
Zoom deep into a phone photo and it crumbles into little blocks. This shows that photographs are stored as:
options: Raster data built from grid cells

subtopics.title: The Chalk Circle Around the Beehive

questions.question: The chalk circle drawn around the beehive so nobody plays inside it works exactly like a GIS:
options: Buffer — a zone with an edge that lets the inside be treated differently

questions.question: An exam map shows a strip of empty land between houses and a river. The best explanation is:
options: The mapmaker forgot to draw that strip
A buffer keeps development out of the flood-prone strip
The printer ran out of ink

questions.question: Typing a song name into a music app and letting it fetch every matching track is the everyday version of:
options: A query searching a database for features that satisfy a condition

questions.question: Before any searching can work, the town's property lists, photos and measurements must first be:
options: Integrated into one system on the same coordinate grid

subtopics.title: Pixels, Zooming In and Free Marks

questions.question: A zoomed-in photo of the scoreboard turns into fuzzy blocks because:
options: The scoreboard moved during the photo
The image holds too few pixels for that much zoom — low resolution

questions.question: The memorandum's expected answer for making an unclear orthophoto area easier to read is:
options: Look at it from further away

questions.question: Which set pairs each GIS idea with its everyday picture correctly?
options: Layers — burger; buffer — chalk circle; query — music-app search; resolution — pixel sharpness
Layers — chalk circle; buffer — burger; query — pixel; resolution — search
Layers — pixels; buffer — search; query — burger; resolution — chalk circle
Layers — search; buffer — pixels; query — chalk circle; resolution — burger

questions.question: The GIS block at the end of the mapwork paper is worth roughly:
options: Seven marks, mostly definitions and short applications
